newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau hotel escapes second bomb attack in week.
newsitem.headline: Macau hotel escapes second bomb attack in week.

text.p: A Macau hotel narrowly escaped its second bomb attack in a week on Thursday when a device was hurled through a window but failed to explode, an official said.
The bomb was thrown through a restaurant window in the New Century Hotel on the Portuguese-run enclave's Taipa island.
"The explosive device was thrown through a window of a restaurant in New Century Hotel this morning," Luis Wong, an official at the Macau Government Information Service, told local radio.
He said it did not go off and there were no injures.
Police were investigating the incident, which came just a week after they used a robot to detonate an explosive device found under a tour bus outside the same 600-room hotel.
The China-funded hotel was recently taken over by a local consortium that planned to open a casino.
Recent reports from Macau have said rival triad gangs are about to renew a gangland turf war.
A spate of firebombings, knifings and drive-by shootings has claimed at least 16 lives this year in the territory, which returns to Chinese rule in 1999.
The gangs are fighting over shares in illegal loansharking and protection rackets linked to the legal casino business, Macau's biggest industry.
The number of tourists visiting Macau fell 10 percent in May from the same month of 1996.
